title: close-phase judges a landing by the phase the merge brings in
desiredOutcome: a phase signed off on its branch lands and is cleaned up in one close-phase run from the parent, its preview says the same, and a re-run never moves mergedAt

findings.issue: the landed-and-gone early return fired on a composed branch name, so another identity could be told 'nothing left to do' while the real branch held unmerged work
findings.resolution: fixed in P65.2-iy2 (5511a12): only a recorded or passed branch; a composed one exits 4 asking for --branch

findings.issue: the worktree-signoff landing was proven single-file only and never in --dry-run
findings.resolution: fixed in P65.2-iy2 (5511a12): g16c previews first, g16d is the sharded variant

review.outcome: matches the desired outcome; two findings (one med, one low) fixed in P65.2-iy2

summary: close-phase now judges a landing by the phase the merge brings in: the cleanup's settlement is read from the branch tip, where the sign-off was committed, so a phase signed off in its worktree lands and is cleaned up in one run from the parent's tree, and its dry-run previews the same. A recorded mergedAt is kept, a landed phase whose recorded branch is gone is reported as landed, and a composed name is never taken as proof a branch is gone. The commit reader moved into _manifest_io beside its loader; the composed name goes through _branch.phase_answer with git user.name. Desired outcome met, proven end to end on both layouts (g16c, g16d). Fixes BUG-8, found landing P64. Reviewed in phase mode (two findings, fixed); the phase gate ran green with the tree unchanged; the invariant check found no breach.

tasks.title: Fix BUG-8: close-phase judges cleanup by the phase as it stood before its own merge
tasks.description: Repro: sign off a phase in its linked worktree, then run close-phase.py <plan> <phase> --project <parent worktree> from the parent. Expected: the merge lands and the cleanup is judged against the phase as the merge left it (signed off and merged), so the worktree and branch are removed in one run. Actual: 'not done: phase P64 is pending, not done - sign-off has not passed'; a second run is needed, and it re-stamps mergedAt with its own time.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_close_phase.py: repro that FAILS on current code - a phase signed off on its branch is refused cleanup as pending when landed from the parent
tools/check-git-pipeline.py: a worktree phase lands and is cleaned up in one run, and a re-run keeps mergedAt

outcome.technical: met - settlement from the branch tip, kept mergedAt, landed-and-gone exit 0, one composed name; g16c/s4/r3b red first
outcome.descriptive: A phase signed off in its own worktree now lands and is cleaned up in one close-phase run from the main tree, and running it again never changes when the merge is recorded as having happened.

tasks.title: Sign-off review findings: the landed-and-gone answer trusts only a recorded branch, and the landing is proven sharded and in preview
tasks.description: P65 sign-off review: (1) the 'landed and gone' early return fires on a COMPOSED name, so with a different git identity it answers 'nothing left to do' about a branch that was never called that, while the real one may hold unmerged work; (2) phase_as_landed is proven only single-file and never in --dry-run.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test_close_phase.py: a composed branch name that does not exist is not taken as the landed branch being gone
tools/check-git-pipeline.py: the worktree-signoff landing on the sharded layout, and its dry-run preview

outcome.technical: met - landed-and-gone only on a recorded/passed branch, exit 4 on a composed one; g16c preview + g16d sharded; red first
outcome.descriptive: close-phase no longer says a phase is finished on the strength of a guessed branch name, and the one-run landing is proven for both plan layouts and in preview.
